You shall make twisted tassels upon the four edges of your outer garments wherewith you cover yourself.
And if a man takes a wife, and dwells with her as husband, and hates her,
and brings charges against her as a pretext, and gives her an evil name, and says: I took this woman, and when I came unto her, I did not find the tokens of her virginity,
then the father of the young woman and her mother shall take and bring forth the tokens of her virginity unto the elders at the gate.
And the father of the young woman shall say unto the elders: I gave this my daughter unto this man for a wife, and he has hated her;

and behold, he brings charges against her as a pretext, saying: I did not find the tokens of your daughter’s virginity. Yet these are the tokens of my daughter’s virginity. And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.
And the elders of that city shall take that man and chasten him.

And they shall fine him a hundred shekels, and give them unto the father of the young woman, because he has brought an evil name upon a virgin of Israel; and she shall be his wife, and he may not put her away all his days.
But if this matter is true, and the tokens of the young woman’s virginity are not found,

then they shall bring forth the young woman unto the doors of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones, and she shall die; for she has wrought folly among the sons of Israel, bringing harlotry into her father’s house. And you shall remove the evil one from among yourselves.
And if a man is found lying with a woman married unto a husband, you shall put both of them to death, the man who lay with the woman, and the woman; and you shall remove the evil one from Israel.
And if a young woman, a virgin, is betrothed unto a man, and a man finds her in the city and lies with her,

you shall bring both of them forth unto the gate of their city, and they shall be stoned with stones and shall die: the young woman, because she did not cry out in the city, and the man, because he violated his neighbour’s wife. And you shall remove the evil one from among yourselves.
But if a man finds the betrothed young woman in the field, and forces her and lies with her, you shall put to death only the man who lay with her.
And unto the young woman you shall do nothing; there is in her no sin deserving death. For as when a man rises against his neighbour and slays him, so is this matter.
For he found her in the field; the betrothed young woman cried out, and there was none to help her.
And if a man finds a young woman, a virgin who is not betrothed, and forces her and lies with her, and he is found out,
the man who lay with her shall give unto the father of the young woman fifty silver didrachmas, and she shall be his wife, because he violated her; he may not put her away all his days.
A man shall not take his father’s wife or uncover his father’s covering.
He whose testicles are crushed, or whose organ is cut off, shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
One born of a prostitute shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter the assembly of the Lord; even unto the tenth generation he shall not enter the assembly of the Lord, even for ever,
because they did not meet you with bread and water in the way, when you came forth out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam son of Beor, from Mesopotamia, to curse you.
And the Lord your God would not hearken unto Balaam; and the Lord your God turned the curses into a blessing, because the Lord your God loved you.
You shall not speak peace unto them, nor seek their advantage, all your days for ever.
You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother; you shall not abhor an Egyptian, for you were a resident alien in his land.
The sons born unto them shall enter the assembly of the Lord in the third generation.
And when you go forth to encamp against your enemies, you shall keep yourself from every evil thing.
If there is among you a man who is not clean by reason of a discharge in the night, he shall go forth outside the camp, and shall not enter the camp.
And it shall be, toward evening, that he shall wash his body with water; and when the sun is set, he shall enter the camp.
And you shall have a place outside the camp, whither you shall go forth.
And you shall have a peg upon your belt; and when you squat outside, you shall dig therewith, and turn and cover your excrement with it.

For the Lord your God walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you, and to give your enemy before you; therefore your camp shall be holy, that no indecent thing be seen among you, and He turn away from you.
You shall not deliver unto his master a slave who has come unto you from his master.
He shall dwell with you; he shall dwell among you in any place that pleases him. You shall not afflict him.

There shall be no prostitute among the daughters of Israel, neither shall there be one who practises prostitution among the sons of Israel. There shall be no woman who performs initiation rites among the daughters of Israel, neither shall there be an initiated man among the sons of Israel.
You shall not bring the hire of a prostitute, nor the price of a dog, into the house of the Lord your God for any vow; for both are an abomination unto the Lord your God.
You shall not charge your brother interest on silver, nor interest on food, nor interest on anything which you lend.
Unto a foreigner you may lend at interest, but unto your brother you shall not lend at interest; that the Lord your God may bless you in all your works upon the land whither you go to inherit it.
And if you vow a vow unto the Lord your God, you shall not delay to pay it; for the Lord your God shall surely require it of you, and there shall be sin upon you.
But if you do not desire to vow, there is no sin upon you.
That which proceeds through your lips you shall keep and do, as you have vowed a gift unto the Lord your God, which you have spoken with your mouth.
And if you enter your neighbour’s harvest, you may gather heads of grain with your hands; but you shall not put a sickle unto your neighbour’s harvest.
And if you enter your neighbour’s vineyard, you may eat grapes until your soul is filled; but you shall put none in a vessel.

And if a man takes a wife and dwells with her as husband, and she finds no favour in his sight, because he has found some unseemly thing in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, and gives it into her hands, and sends her forth out of his house,
and she departs and becomes another man’s wife,

and the latter husband hates her, and writes her a certificate of divorce, and gives it into her hands, and sends her forth out of his house, or if the latter husband who took her to be his wife dies,

her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after she has been defiled; for it is an abomination before the Lord your God. And you shall not defile the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.
And if a man has newly taken a wife, he shall not go forth unto war, neither shall any duty be laid upon him. He shall be free in his house one year, and shall gladden his wife whom he has taken.
You shall not take a mill or its upper stone in pledge, for he who does so takes a life in pledge.
And if a man is caught stealing one of his brethren, of the sons of Israel, and he subjugates him and sells him, that thief shall die; and you shall remove the evil one from among yourselves.

Take heed unto yourself concerning the affliction of leprosy. You shall take diligent heed to do according to all the law which the Levitical priests shall declare unto you; as I commanded you, take heed to do.
Remember what the Lord your God did unto Miriam in the way, when you came forth out of Egypt.
If your neighbour owes a debt, any debt whatsoever, you shall not enter his house to take his pledge.
You shall stand outside, and the man who owes you the loan shall bring forth the pledge unto you.
And if the man is poor, you shall not sleep with his pledge in your keeping.
You shall surely restore his pledge at the setting of the sun, that he may sleep in his garment and bless you; and it shall be mercy unto you before the Lord your God.
You shall not withhold the wages of the poor and needy, whether of your brethren or of the sojourners within your cities.
On the same day you shall pay his wages; the sun shall not go down upon them, for he is poor and sets his hope upon them; lest he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be sin upon you.
Fathers shall not die for children, and sons shall not die for fathers. Each shall die for his own sin.
You shall not pervert the judgment of the sojourner, or of the orphan, or of the widow; neither shall you take a widow’s garment in pledge.
And you shall remember that you were a household slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you thence; therefore I command you to do this thing.

And when you reap your harvest in your field, and forget a sheaf in your field, you shall not return to take it. It shall be for the poor, and for the sojourner, and for the orphan, and for the widow; that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works of your hands.

And when you gather your olives, you shall not return to glean what remains behind you. It shall be for the sojourner, and for the orphan, and for the widow. And you shall remember that you were a household slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.
And when you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean it afterward; it shall be for the sojourner, and for the orphan, and for the widow.
And you shall remember that you were a household slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.
And if there is a dispute between men, and they come unto judgment, and the judges judge them, and justify the righteous, and condemn the ungodly,
then it shall be, if the ungodly man is worthy of stripes, that you shall seat him before the judges, and they shall scourge him before them, by number according to his ungodliness.
They shall give him forty stripes, and shall not add thereto; lest, if they add more stripes beyond these, your brother be dishonoured before you.
You shall not muzzle an ox when it treads out the grain.

And if brethren dwell together, and one of them dies, and has no seed, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside unto a man who is not near of kin. Her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her unto himself for a wife, and dwell with her as husband.
And it shall be, that the child whom she bears shall be established in the name of the dead, and his name shall not be blotted out of Israel.

And if the man will not take his brother’s wife, the woman shall go up unto the gate, unto the elders, and say: My husband’s brother will not raise up his brother’s name in Israel; my husband’s brother has refused.
And the elders of his city shall call him, and speak unto him; and if he stands and says: I will not take her,

then his brother’s wife shall draw near before the elders, and loose one sandal from his foot, and spit in his face, and answer and say: Thus shall they do unto the man who will not build up his brother’s house.
And his name shall be called in Israel: The House of Him Whose Sandal Was Loosed.
And if men strive together, a man with his brother, and the wife of one draws near to deliver her husband out of the hand of him that strikes him, and puts forth her hand, and seizes his testicles,
you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not spare her.
You shall not have in your pouch differing weights, a great and a small.
You shall not have in your house differing measures, a great and a small.
You shall have a true and just weight, and you shall have a true and just measure, that your days may be long upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.
For everyone who does these things, everyone who does injustice, is an abomination unto the Lord your God.
Remember what Amalek did unto you in the way, when you came forth out of Egypt,
how he withstood you in the way, and smote your rear, those who were weary behind you, when you were hungry and weary; and he did not fear God.

And it shall be, when the Lord your God gives you rest from all your enemies round about you, in the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession to inherit, that you shall blot out the name of Amalek from under heaven. You shall not forget.
And it shall be, when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, and inherit it, and dwell therein,

that you shall take of the firstfruits of the produce of your land which the Lord your God gives you, and put it in a basket, and go unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.

And you shall come unto the priest who shall be in those days, and say unto him: I declare this day unto the Lord my God, that I have come into the land which the Lord sware unto our fathers to give us.
And the priest shall take the basket out of your hands, and set it before the altar of the Lord your God.

And you shall answer and say before the Lord your God: My father forsook Syria, and went down into Egypt, and sojourned there, few in number; and there he became a great nation, and a multitude numerous and great.
And the Egyptians afflicted us, and humbled us, and laid hard labours upon us.
And we cried unto the Lord, the God of our fathers; and the Lord heard our voice, and saw our humiliation, and our toil, and our distress.
And the Lord Himself brought us forth out of Egypt with great strength, and with a mighty hand, and with His uplifted arm, and with great visions, and with signs, and with wonders.
And He brought us unto this place, and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the produce of the land which Thou hast given me, O Lord, a land flowing with milk and honey. And you shall set them before the Lord your God, and bow down there before the Lord your God.
And you shall rejoice in all the good things which the Lord your God has given unto you and unto your house, you, and the Levite, and the sojourner among you.

And when you have finished tithing all the tithe of the produce of your land in the third year, you shall give the second tithe unto the Levite, and unto the sojourner, and unto the orphan, and unto the widow; and they shall eat within your cities and be filled.

And you shall say before the Lord your God: I have cleared the holy things out of my house, and have given them unto the Levite, and unto the sojourner, and unto the orphan, and unto the widow, according to all Thy commandments which Thou hast commanded me. I have not transgressed Thy commandment, neither have I forgotten it.

And I have not eaten thereof in my mourning, neither have I offered thereof for an unclean use, nor given thereof unto the dead. I have hearkened unto the voice of the Lord my God; I have done according to all that Thou hast commanded me.
Look down from Thy holy house, from heaven, and bless Thy people Israel, and the land which Thou hast given them, as Thou didst swear unto our fathers to give us a land flowing with milk and honey.
This day the Lord your God has commanded you to do all these ordinances and judgments; and you shall keep and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
You have chosen God this day to be your God, and to walk in His ways, and to keep His ordinances and His judgments, and to hearken unto His voice.
And the Lord has chosen you this day to be unto Him a people for His own possession, as He has spoken unto you, to keep all His commandments,
and to be above all the nations, as He has made you renowned, and a boast, and glorious, that you should be a holy people unto the Lord your God, as He has spoken.
And Moses and the elders of Israel commanded, saying: Keep all these commandments which I command you this day.
And it shall be, in the day when you pass over the Jordan into the land which the Lord your God gives you, that you shall set up great stones for yourself, and plaster them with plaster.

And you shall write upon the stones all the words of this law, when you pass over the Jordan, when you enter the land which the Lord, the God of your fathers, gives you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, has spoken unto you.
And it shall be, when you pass over the Jordan, that you shall set up these stones, which I command you this day, upon Mount Ebal; and you shall plaster them with plaster.
And you shall build there an altar unto the Lord your God, an altar of stones; you shall lay no iron upon them.
You shall build an altar of whole stones unto the Lord your God, and you shall offer thereon whole burnt offerings unto the Lord your God.
And you shall sacrifice there a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord your God, and eat, and be filled, and rejoice before the Lord your God.
And you shall write upon the stones all this law very plainly.
And Moses and the Levitical priests spoke unto all Israel, saying: Keep silence, and hear, O Israel; this day you have become a people unto the Lord your God.
And you shall hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, and do all His commandments and His ordinances which I command you this day.
And Moses commanded the people in that day, saying:
These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people after crossing the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
And these shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
And the Levites shall answer and say unto all Israel with a loud voice:

Cursed is the man who makes a graven and molten image, an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of a craftsman, and sets it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say: So be it.
Cursed is he who dishonours his father or his mother. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who removes his neighbour’s boundaries. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who leads the blind astray in the way. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who perverts the judgment of the sojourner, and of the orphan, and of the widow. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who lies with his father’s wife, for he has uncovered his father’s covering. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who lies with any beast. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who lies with his mother-in-law. And all the people shall say: So be it. Cursed is he who lies with his wife’s sister. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who strikes his neighbour treacherously. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who takes a bribe to slay an innocent life. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is every man who does not continue in all the words of this law, to do them. And all the people shall say: So be it.

And it shall be, when you pass over the Jordan into the land which the Lord your God gives you, if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments which I command you this day, that the Lord your God shall set you above all the nations of the earth.
And all these blessings shall come upon you, and find you, if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.
Blessed are you in the city, and blessed are you in the field.
Blessed are the offspring of your womb, and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Blessed are your storehouses and your reserves.
Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out.
The Lord your God deliver your enemies who rise against you, crushed before your face. By one way shall they come out against you, and by seven ways shall they flee before you.
The Lord send His blessing upon you in your storerooms, and in all that you put your hand unto, upon the land which the Lord your God gives you.
The Lord your God establish you unto Himself a holy people, as He sware unto your fathers, if you hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, and walk in His ways.
And all the nations of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you.

And the Lord your God shall multiply you in good things, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your cattle, upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give you.

The Lord open unto you His good treasure, heaven, to give rain unto your land in its season, and to bless all the works of your hands. And you shall lend unto many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.
The Lord your God make you the head, and not the tail; and you shall be above, and not beneath, if you hearken unto the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you this day to keep and do.
You shall not turn aside from any of the words which I command you this day, to the right hand or to the left, to go after other gods and serve them.

And it shall be, if you do not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments which I command you this day, that all these curses shall come upon you, and overtake you.
Cursed are you in the city, and cursed are you in the field.
Cursed are your storehouses and your reserves.
Cursed are the offspring of your womb, and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Cursed are you when you go out, and cursed are you when you come in.

The Lord send upon you want, and famine, and wasting, in all that you put your hand unto, whatsoever you do, until He destroys you, and causes you to perish speedily, because of your evil practices, because you have forsaken Me.
The Lord make death cleave unto you, until He consumes you from the land whither you go to inherit it.
The Lord smite you with destitution, and fever, and chills, and inflammation, and slaughter, and wind blight, and pallor; and they shall pursue you until they destroy you.
And the heaven above your head shall be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron.
The Lord give dust for the rain of your land; and earth shall descend upon you from heaven, until He wears you away, and until He destroys you.

The Lord give you over to slaughter before your enemies. You shall go forth by one way against them, and you shall flee by seven ways before them; and you shall be scattered among all the kingdoms of the earth.
And your dead shall be food for the birds of heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and there shall be none to drive them away.
The Lord smite you with the Egyptian ulcer upon the buttocks, and with grievous scab, and with itching, so that you cannot be healed.
The Lord smite you with madness, and with blindness, and with bewilderment of mind.
And you shall grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and He shall not prosper your ways; and you shall be wronged and plundered all your days, and there shall be none to help you.
You shall take a wife, and another man shall have her; you shall build a house, and shall not dwell therein; you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not gather its fruit.

Your calf shall be slaughtered before your eyes, and you shall not eat thereof; your donkey shall be seized from you, and shall not be restored unto you; your sheep shall be given unto your enemies, and there shall be none to help you.
Your sons and your daughters shall be given unto another nation, and your eyes shall look upon them and waste away; and your hand shall have no strength.
A nation which you do not know shall consume the yield of your land and all your labours; and you shall be wronged and crushed all your days.
And you shall be driven mad by the sights which your eyes shall see.
The Lord smite you upon the knees and upon the legs with a grievous ulcer, so that you cannot be healed, from the soles of your feet unto the crown of your head.
The Lord lead you, and your rulers whom you shall set over yourself, unto a nation which neither you nor your fathers have known; and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone.
And there you shall become a riddle, and a parable, and a tale among all the nations whither the Lord shall lead you.
You shall carry much seed into the field, and gather little; for the locust shall devour it.
You shall plant a vineyard and dress it, but shall neither drink wine nor rejoice in it; for the worm shall devour it.
You shall have olive trees throughout all your borders, but shall not anoint yourself with oil; for your olives shall fall away.
You shall beget sons and daughters, but they shall not be yours; for they shall go into captivity.
Blight shall consume all your trees and the produce of your land.
The sojourner who is among you shall rise above you higher and higher; but you shall descend lower and lower.
He shall lend unto you, but you shall not lend unto him; he shall be the head, and you shall be the tail.

And all these curses shall come upon you, and pursue you, and overtake you, until He destroys you, and until He causes you to perish; for you did not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep His commandments and His ordinances which He commanded you.
And they shall be signs and wonders upon you and upon your seed for ever,
because you did not serve the Lord your God with gladness and a good heart, for the abundance of all things.

And you shall serve your enemies whom the Lord shall send against you, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things; and He shall put an iron collar upon your neck, until He destroys you.
The Lord shall bring against you a nation from afar, from the end of the earth, as the swooping of an eagle, a nation whose speech you shall not understand,
a nation shameless of countenance, which shall not regard the face of the aged, nor have mercy upon the young.

And it shall consume the offspring of your cattle and the produce of your land, leaving you neither grain, nor wine, nor oil, nor the herds of your cattle, nor the flocks of your sheep, until it destroys you.

And it shall wear you down in all your cities, until your high and fortified walls wherein you trust are cast down throughout all your land; and it shall afflict you in all your cities which the Lord your God has given you.

And you shall eat the offspring of your womb, the flesh of your sons and of your daughters whom the Lord your God has given you, in your straitness and in your distress wherewith your enemy shall afflict you.
The tender and most delicate man among you shall look grudgingly upon his brother, and the wife of his bosom, and the children who remain unto him,
begrudging any of them the flesh of his children which he eats, because nothing is left unto him, in your straitness and in your distress wherewith your enemies shall afflict you in all your cities.

And the tender and most delicate woman among you, whose foot has never ventured to tread upon the earth because of her delicacy and tenderness, shall look grudgingly upon the husband of her bosom, and her son, and her daughter,

and upon her afterbirth which comes forth from between her thighs, and the child whom she bears; for she shall eat them secretly for want of all things, in your straitness and in your distress wherewith your enemy shall afflict you in all your cities.
If you do not hearken to do all the words of this law written in this book, to fear this honoured and wondrous name, the Lord your God,
then the Lord shall make your plagues and the plagues of your seed extraordinary, plagues great and astonishing, and diseases grievous and enduring.
And He shall bring back upon you all the grievous suffering of Egypt which you dreaded; and they shall cleave unto you.
And every infirmity, and every plague which is not written in the book of this law, shall the Lord bring upon you, until He destroys you.
And you shall be left few in number, whereas you were as the stars of heaven in multitude, because you did not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.

And it shall be, as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so shall the Lord rejoice over you to destroy you; and you shall be removed from the land whither you go to inherit it.

And the Lord your God shall scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth unto the other; and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers have known.

And among those nations He shall give you no rest, neither shall there be a resting place for the sole of your foot; and the Lord shall give you there a faint heart, and failing eyes, and a wasting soul.
And your life shall hang before your eyes, and you shall fear day and night, and shall have no assurance of your life.

In the morning you shall say: Would that it were evening! And at evening you shall say: Would that it were morning! Because of the fear of your heart wherewith you shall fear, and the sights of your eyes which you shall see.

And the Lord shall bring you back into Egypt in ships, and by the way whereof I said: You shall see it no more. And there shall you be sold unto your enemies for male slaves and female slaves, and there shall be none to buy.
These are the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses to establish with the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant which He made with them in Horeb.
And Moses called all the sons of Israel, and said unto them, You have seen all that the Lord did in the land of Egypt before you unto Pharaoh, and unto his servants, and unto all his land:
the great trials which your eyes have seen, the signs, and those great wonders.
And the Lord God has not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day.
And He led you forty years in the wilderness; your garments did not grow old, and your sandals did not wear away from your feet.
You ate no bread, and drank no wine or strong drink, that you might know that He is the Lord your God.
And you came unto this place; and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us in battle, and we smote them.
And we took their land, and I gave it as an inheritance unto Reuben, and unto Gad, and unto the half tribe of Manasseh.
And you shall take heed to do all the words of this covenant, that you may understand all that you shall do.
You stand all this day before the Lord your God: your tribal chiefs, and your elders, and your judges, and your recording officers, every man of Israel,
your wives, and your children, and the sojourner who is in the midst of your camp, from your woodcutter unto your water carrier,
that you may enter into the covenant of the Lord your God, and into His curses, which the Lord your God covenants with you this day;
that He may establish you unto Himself for a people, and He shall be your God, as He said unto you, and as He sware unto your fathers, Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob.
And not with you alone do I make this covenant and this curse,
but also with those who are here with us this day before the Lord your God, and with those who are not here with us this day.
For you know how we dwelt in the land of Egypt, and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed.
And you saw their abominations and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which are among them.

Is there among you a man, or woman, or family, or tribe, whose mind has turned aside from the Lord your God, to go and serve the gods of those nations? Is there among you a root springing up in gall and bitterness?

And it shall be, if he hears the words of this curse and pronounces a blessing in his heart, saying, May it be well with me, though I walk in the wandering of my heart—so that the sinner may not destroy the guiltless with him—

God will in no wise be willing to be merciful unto him; but then the anger of the Lord and His jealousy shall blaze against that man, and all the curses of this covenant which are written in this book of the law shall cleave unto him, and the Lord shall blot out his name from under heaven.
And the Lord shall set him apart for evils from all the sons of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant which are written in this book of the law.

And the generation to come, your sons who shall arise after you, and the foreigner who shall come from a far land, shall speak; and they shall see the plagues of that land and its diseases, which the Lord has sent upon it—

sulfur and salt, burned over; all its land shall neither be sown nor sprout, neither shall any green thing grow upon it, as at the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew in wrath and anger—
and all the nations shall say, Why has the Lord done thus unto this land? What does this great heat of anger mean?
And they shall say, Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which He made with their fathers when He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt;
and they went and served other gods, and bowed down unto them, whom they did not know, and whom He had not allotted unto them.
And the Lord was kindled in wrath against that land, to bring upon it all the curses which are written in this book of the law.
And the Lord removed them from their land in wrath, and anger, and exceeding great indignation, and cast them into another land, as it is now.
The hidden things belong unto the Lord our God; but the things revealed belong unto us and unto our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.

And it shall be, when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse which I have set before your face, and you receive them into your heart among all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you,
and you return unto the Lord your God, and obey His voice according to all that I command you this day, with all your heart and with all your soul,
then the Lord shall heal your sins, and have mercy upon you, and shall gather you again from all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you.
If your dispersion is from one end of heaven unto the other end of heaven, from thence shall the Lord your God gather you, and from thence shall the Lord your God take you.
And the Lord your God shall bring you into the land which your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it; and He shall do you good, and make you more numerous than your fathers.
And the Lord shall thoroughly cleanse your heart, and the heart of your seed, to love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live.
And the Lord your God shall lay these curses upon your enemies, and upon them that hate you, who pursued you.
And you shall return, and obey the voice of the Lord your God, and do His commandments, all that I command you this day.

And the Lord your God shall care greatly for you in every work of your hands, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your cattle; for the Lord your God shall again rejoice over you for good, as He rejoiced over your fathers,

if you obey the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and to do all His commandments, and His ordinances, and His judgments which are written in this book of the law; if you return unto the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
For this commandment which I command you this day is not excessively burdensome, neither is it far from you.
It is not in heaven above, that you should say, Who shall ascend for us into heaven, and fetch it for us, that we may hear it and do it?
Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, Who shall cross for us unto the other side of the sea, and fetch it for us, and make us hear it, that we may do it?
The word is very near you, in your mouth, and in your heart, and in your hands, that you may do it.
Behold, I have set before your face this day life and death, good and evil.

If you obey the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His ordinances and His judgments, then you shall live and be many; and the Lord your God shall bless you in all the land into which you go to inherit it.
And if your heart turns aside, and you will not hearken, and you are led astray to bow down unto other gods and serve them,
I declare unto you this day that you shall surely perish, and you shall in no wise be long-lived upon the land which the Lord your God gives you, into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.
I call heaven and earth to witness unto you this day: I have set before your face life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, that you and your seed may live,

to love the Lord your God, to obey His voice, and to cleave unto Him; for this is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers, Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them.
And Moses finished speaking all these words unto all the sons of Israel.
And he said unto them, I am a hundred and twenty years old this day; I shall no longer be able to go in and come out. And the Lord said unto me, You shall not cross this Jordan.

The Lord your God, who goes before your face, shall Himself destroy these nations from before your face, and you shall take possession of them; and Joshua shall go before your face, as the Lord has spoken.
And the Lord shall do unto them as He did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, and unto their land, when He destroyed them.
And the Lord delivered them unto you, and you shall do unto them as I commanded you.

Be courageous and strong; fear not, neither be fainthearted, neither be terrified before their face; for the Lord your God, who goes before you, is with you and among you. He will in no wise fail you, neither will He forsake you.

And Moses called Joshua, and said unto him before all Israel, Be courageous and strong; for you shall go before the face of this people into the land which the Lord sware unto our fathers to give unto them, and you shall give it unto them for an inheritance.
And the Lord who goes with you will not fail you, neither will He forsake you; fear not, neither be fainthearted.
And Moses wrote the words of this law in a book, and gave it unto the priests, the sons of Levi, who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and unto the elders of the sons of Israel.
And Moses commanded them in that day, saying, After seven years, at the appointed time of the year of release, at the Feast of the Pitching of Tents,
when all Israel comes together to appear before the Lord your God in the place which the Lord shall choose, you shall read this law before all Israel in their hearing.

Gather the people, the men, and the women, and the children, and the sojourner who is in your cities, that they may hear, and that they may learn to fear the Lord your God; and they shall hearken to do all the words of this law.
And their sons, who do not know, shall hear and learn to fear the Lord your God all the days that they live upon the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.

And the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, the days of your death draw near; call Joshua, and stand beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and I will command him. And Moses and Joshua went unto the Tent of Testimony, and stood beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord descended in a cloud, and stood beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony; and the pillar of the cloud stood beside the doors of the Tent.

And the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers; and this people shall arise and go a-whoring after the foreign gods of the land into which it goes; and they shall forsake Me, and break My covenant which I made with them.

And I will be kindled in wrath against them in that day, and will forsake them, and turn My face from them; and the people shall be devoured, and many evils and afflictions shall find it. And it shall say in that day, Because the Lord my God is not within me, these evils have found me.
But I will surely turn My face from them in that day, because of all the wickedness which they have done, for they have turned unto foreign gods.
And now write the words of this song, and teach it unto the sons of Israel, and put it in their mouth, that this song may be a witness for Me among the sons of Israel.

For I will bring them into the good land which I sware unto their fathers to give unto them, a land flowing with milk and honey; and they shall eat, and be filled, and be sated; and they shall turn unto foreign gods, and serve them, and provoke Me, and break My covenant.

And this song shall stand against them, bearing witness before their face; for it shall in no wise be forgotten from their mouth, nor from the mouth of their seed. For I know their wickedness, all that they do here this day, before I bring them into the good land which I sware unto their fathers.
And Moses wrote this song in that day, and taught it unto the sons of Israel.
And Moses commanded Joshua, and said unto him, Be courageous and strong; for you shall bring the sons of Israel into the land which the Lord sware unto them, and He shall be with you.
And when Moses had finished writing all the words of this law in a book, even unto the end,
he commanded the Levites who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying,
Take this book of the law, and lay it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God; and it shall be there for a witness against you.
For I know your provocation and your stiff neck; for while I yet live with you this day, you have been provoking God: how much more after my death!
Gather unto me your tribal chiefs, and your elders, and your judges, and your recording officers, that I may speak all these words in their hearing, and call heaven and earth to witness unto them.

For I know that after my death you shall deal utterly lawlessly, and turn aside from the way which I commanded you; and evils shall meet you in the latter days, because you shall do that which is evil before the Lord, to provoke Him to anger by the works of your hands.
And Moses spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song, even unto the end:
Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak; and let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
Let my utterance be awaited as the rain, and let my words descend as the dew, as a shower upon the grass, and as snow upon the herbage.
For I have called upon the name of the Lord; ascribe greatness unto our God.
God—true are His works, and all His ways are judgments; a faithful God, and there is no unrighteousness; righteous and holy is the Lord.
Blemished children, not His, have sinned—a crooked and perverse generation.
Do you thus repay the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? Is not He Himself your Father, who acquired you, and made you, and created you?
Remember the days of old; consider the years of generation upon generation. Ask your father, and he shall declare unto you; your elders, and they shall tell you.
When the Most High divided the nations, when He scattered the sons of Adam, He set the bounds of the nations according to the number of the angels of God.
And His people Jacob became the portion of the Lord; Israel, the measured lot of His inheritance.
He sustained him in a wilderness land, in the thirst of burning heat, in a waterless place; He compassed him about, and instructed him, and kept him as the pupil of an eye.
As an eagle would shelter its nest, it yearned over its young; spreading its wings, it received them, and took them up upon its back.
The Lord alone led them, and there was no foreign god with them.
He brought them up upon the strength of the earth, and fed them the produce of the fields; they sucked honey out of the rock, and oil out of the solid rock,
butter of cattle and milk of sheep, with the fat of lambs and rams, young bulls and goats, with the fat of the kernels of wheat; and they drank wine, the blood of the grape.
And Jacob ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked; he grew fat, he grew thick, he grew broad; and he forsook God who made him, and departed from God his Saviour.
They provoked Me with foreign gods; with their abominations they embittered Me.
They sacrificed unto demons, and not unto God, unto gods whom they did not know; new ones, lately come, whom their fathers did not know.
You forsook God who begat you, and forgot God who nourishes you.
And the Lord saw, and was jealous, and was provoked by the anger of His sons and daughters.
And He said, I will turn My face from them, and show what shall befall them at the last; for they are a perverse generation, sons in whom is no faithfulness.

They made Me jealous with that which is no god; they provoked Me to anger with their idols. And I will make them jealous with that which is no nation; with a nation without understanding will I provoke them to anger.
For a fire has been kindled out of My wrath; it shall burn unto Hades beneath, devour the earth and its produce, and set ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
I will gather evils against them, and spend My arrows upon them.

They shall waste away with hunger, and be devoured by birds, and suffer incurable backward-bending spasms; I will send against them the teeth of wild beasts, with the fury of things that crawl upon the ground.
Without, the sword shall bereave them; and from the inner chambers, terror: the young man together with the maiden, the nursing child with the aged elder.
I said, I will scatter them; I will make their remembrance cease from among men,
were it not for the wrath of enemies, lest they endure long, and lest the adversaries join in the attack; lest they say, Our hand is exalted, and the Lord has not done all these things.
For it is a nation that has lost counsel, and there is no knowledge in them.
They did not have the wisdom to understand these things; let them receive them for the time to come.
How shall one pursue a thousand, and two put tens of thousands to flight, unless God had sold them, and the Lord had delivered them up?
For their gods are not as our God; and our enemies are without understanding.
For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and their tendril is of Gomorrah; their grape is a grape of gall, their cluster is bitterness.
Their wine is the venom of serpents, and the incurable venom of asps.
Behold, are not these things gathered with Me, and sealed in My treasuries?
In the day of vengeance I will repay, in the season when their foot shall slip; for the day of their destruction is near, and the things prepared for you are at hand.
For the Lord shall judge His people, and be moved concerning His servants; for He saw them weakened, and failing under assault, and exhausted.
And the Lord said, Where are their gods, in whom they trusted,
whose sacrifices’ fat you ate, and whose drink offerings’ wine you drank? Let them arise and help you, and become your protectors.
See, see that I am, and there is no god beside Me. I will put to death, and make alive; I will smite, and I will heal; and there is none that shall deliver out of My hands.
For I will lift My hand unto heaven, and swear by My right hand, and say, I live for ever.
For I will sharpen My sword as lightning, and My hand shall lay hold of judgment; and I will repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Me will I repay.
I will make My arrows drunk with blood, and My sword shall devour flesh, from the blood of the slain and of captives, from the head of the rulers of the enemies.

Rejoice, O heavens, together with Him, and let all the sons of God worship Him; rejoice, O nations, with His people, and let all the angels of God give Him strength; for He avenges the blood of His sons, and shall avenge and repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Him shall He repay; and the Lord shall thoroughly cleanse the land of His people.
And Moses wrote this song in that day, and taught it unto the sons of Israel. And Moses came in and spoke all the words of this law in the hearing of the people, he and Joshua the son of Nun.
And Moses finished speaking unto all Israel,
and said unto them, Give heed in your heart unto all these words which I testify unto you this day, which you shall command your sons to keep and to do, even all the words of this law.
For this is no empty word unto you; for this is your life, and by this word you shall prolong your days upon the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses in that day, saying,
Go up into this mountain of Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab over against Jericho, and behold the land of Canaan, which I give unto the sons of Israel for a possession.
And die in the mountain whither you go up, and be gathered unto your people, as Aaron your brother died in Mount Hor, and was gathered unto his people;
because you disobeyed My word among the sons of Israel at the water of dispute at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not sanctify Me among the sons of Israel.
For you shall see the land from over against it, but you shall not go in thither.
And this is the blessing wherewith Moses, the man of God, blessed the sons of Israel before his death.
And he said, The Lord has come from Sinai, and appeared unto us from Seir, and hastened from Mount Paran with myriads of Kadesh; at His right hand were angels with Him.
And He spared His people; and all the consecrated ones are under Thy hands; and these are under Thee; and the people received from His words
the law which Moses commanded us, an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob.
And there shall be a ruler in the beloved, when the rulers of the peoples are gathered together with the tribes of Israel.
Let Reuben live, and not die; and let him be many in number.
And this for Judah: Hear, O Lord, the voice of Judah, and let them enter unto his people; his hands shall contend for him, and Thou shalt be a helper against his enemies.
And unto Levi he said, Give unto Levi his manifestations, and his truth unto the holy man, whom they tested in a trial, and reviled at the water of dispute;
who says unto his father and his mother, I have not seen you; and he did not acknowledge his brethren, and disowned his sons. He kept Thine oracles, and preserved Thy covenant.
They shall declare Thine ordinances unto Jacob, and Thy law unto Israel; they shall lay incense in Thy wrath, continually upon Thine altar.
Bless, O Lord, his strength, and accept the works of his hands; break the loin of the enemies who rise against him, and let not them that hate him arise.
And unto Benjamin he said, He who is beloved of the Lord shall dwell in confidence; and God overshadows him all the days, and between his shoulders He rested.
And unto Joseph he said, From the blessing of the Lord is his land, from the seasons of heaven and the dew, and from the springs of the depths beneath,
and in the season of the produce of the sun’s turnings, and from the conjunctions of the months,
and from the summit of the ancient mountains, and from the summit of the everlasting hills,

and in the season of the fullness of the earth. And may the things acceptable unto Him who appeared in the bush come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of him who was glorified among his brethren.

His beauty is that of a firstborn bull; his horns are the horns of a one-horned animal; with them shall he gore the nations together unto the end of the earth. These are the myriads of Ephraim, and these are the thousands of Manasseh.
And unto Zebulun he said, Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going forth; and Issachar, in his dwellings.

They shall destroy nations; and you shall call upon God there, and sacrifice a sacrifice of righteousness; for the wealth of the sea shall nourish you, and the commerce of them that dwell by the coast.
And unto Gad he said, Blessed is He that enlarges Gad; as a lion he rested, having crushed an arm and a ruler.
And he saw his first portion; for there was apportioned the land of rulers gathered together with the leaders of the peoples. The Lord wrought righteousness, and His judgment with Israel.
And unto Dan he said, Dan is a lion’s cub, and shall leap forth from Bashan.
And unto Naphtali he said, Naphtali, a fullness of acceptable things; and let him be filled with blessing from the Lord; he shall inherit the sea and the south.
And unto Asher he said, Asher is blessed with children, and shall be acceptable unto his brethren; he shall dip his foot in oil.
His sandal shall be iron and bronze; and as your days, so shall your strength be.
There is none like the God of the beloved, who rides upon heaven as your helper, the majestic One of the firmament.
And there is shelter from the God of old, and you are under the strength of everlasting arms; and He shall drive out the enemy from before your face, saying, May you perish.
And Israel shall dwell in confidence, alone upon the land of Jacob, with grain and wine; and the heaven for him shall be clouded with dew.

Blessed are you, O Israel! Who is like unto you, a people saved by the Lord? Your helper shall shield you, and the sword is your boast; and your enemies shall lie unto you, and you shall tread upon their neck.
And Moses went up from Araboth of Moab unto Mount Nebo, unto the summit of Pisgah, which is over against Jericho; and the Lord showed him all the land of Gilead unto Dan,
and all the land of Naphtali, and all the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah unto the farthest sea,
and the wilderness, and the country round about Jericho, the city of palms, unto Zoar.

And the Lord said unto Moses, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, saying, I will give it unto your seed. And I have showed it unto your eyes, but you shall not go in thither.
And Moses, the household servant of the Lord, died in the land of Moab by the word of the Lord.
And they buried him in Gai, in the land of Moab, near the house of Peor; and no man knows his burial place unto this day.
And Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eyes were not dimmed, neither were his cheeks wasted away.
And the sons of Israel wept for Moses in Araboth of Moab, at the Jordan over against Jericho, thirty days; and the days of mourning and weeping for Moses were ended.
And Joshua the son of Nun was filled with a spirit of understanding; for Moses had laid his hands upon him; and the sons of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.
And there arose no more a prophet in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,
in all the signs and wonders which the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt unto Pharaoh, and unto his servants, and unto all his land,
the great wonders and the mighty hand which Moses wrought before all Israel.
